A4-02.detail:
This file uses an older map of the genome (GRCh37/hg19), and this analysis needs GRCh38/hg38. The two number the same positions differently, so the file cannot be read as it stands. The header gives chr1 a length of 249,250,621 bases, which is GRCh37's chr1; GRCh38's is 248,956,422.

Converting between them is outside what this analysis does. Convert the file to GRCh38 and upload it again — the input requirements page lists the tools that do this. See docs/input_requirements.md.

warnings: Chromosome names were read in GRCh38's 'chr' form: '1' as 'chr1', '10' as 'chr10', '12' as 'chr12' and 3 more. PharmCAT recognises only names that begin with 'chr'; the positions themselves are unchanged.

A4-06.detail: 'A4-06.bcf' is a BCF file, the binary form of VCF, and this analysis reads text VCF. Convert it to a .vcf (or a compressed .vcf.gz) and upload that; the input requirements page gives the command. See docs/input_requirements.md.

warnings: This file is a gVCF: 445 required positions lie inside reference blocks (records whose END= spans several positions) rather than on rows of their own. PharmCAT reads a position without its own row as not tested, so these count as missing, and genes that need them are reported as Unknown. Export a VCF that gives every required position its own row, then upload it again; the input requirements page gives the commands. See docs/input_requirements.md.

A4-09b.detail: At 1 of the 463 required positions in this file, the REF allele is not GRCh38's: chr10:94781859 (rs4244285, CYP2C19): the file has C, GRCh38 has G. A genotype is read relative to its REF allele, so these rows say something other than what they appear to, and a file that disagrees with GRCh38 anywhere cannot be trusted elsewhere: no drug is assessed from it. Check that the file was produced against GRCh38, with the same reference throughout, and upload it again. See docs/input_requirements.md.
